summary_en: This Phase 3 trial tests T-bren (trastuzumab brengitecan, also listed as BL-M07D1), an antibody drug conjugate, against standard platinum-based chemotherapy. It is for people with HER2-expressing metastatic urothelial (bladder) cancer whose disease progressed on or after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy. T-bren is given into a vein on day 1 of each 21-day cycle at one of two dose levels, while the comparison arm receives gemcitabine on days 1 and 8 plus cisplatin or carboplatin on day 1 of each 21-day cycle; the total duration is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome; it says the study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of T-bren.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 3 evalúa T-bren (trastuzumab brengitecan, también listado como BL-M07D1), un conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco, frente a la quimioterapia estándar a base de platino. Está dirigido a personas con cáncer urotelial (de vejiga) metastásico que expresa HER2 y cuya enfermedad progresó durante o después de una terapia anti-PD-(L)1. T-bren se administra por vena el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, en uno de dos niveles de dosis, mientras que el brazo de comparación recibe gemcitabina los días 1 y 8, más cisplatino o carboplatino el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días; la duración total no se indica. El registro no indica un desenlace primario; señala que el estudio busca evaluar la eficacia y la seguridad de T-bren.
who_for: Metastatic or surgically unresectable urothelial (transitional cell) cancer, confirmed by tests
Disease progressed during or after anti-PD-(L)1-based therapy
HER2 expression confirmed by central laboratory testing
Eligible to receive gemcitabine with cisplatin or carboplatin
At least one measurable lesion, ECOG performance status 0 to 1, and adequate organ and clotting function
not_for: Prior topoisomerase inhibitor-based antibody drug conjugate therapy
Primary brain or spinal tumors, active or untreated brain metastases, or carcinomatous meningitis
Bladder cancer with small cell histology
Clinically significant bleeding or stomach or intestinal perforation within 6 months of randomization
Active autoimmune or inflammatory disease, or current or steroid-treated interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis
